candidate.title: TruSeq RNA Access
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq RNA Access capture-enrichment component depicted in the assigned Illumina poster panel: already prepared stranded RNA-Seq libraries are pooled, hybridized to biotinylated target probes, captured on streptavidin magnetic beads and eluted as a target-containing indexed library ready for cluster generation. The panel does not depict initial RNA-to-library preparation, a probe-derived measurement product, or downstream sequencing. No alternative workflow, protocol version or primary-paper association is supplied.

operations.label: Hybridize probes to targets
operations.description: Add the biotinylated target probe to the library pool and hybridize it to a complementary target region. A free library molecule becomes a probe-associated library molecule with a biotin capture handle.

operations.label: Elute
operations.description: Release the captured target-containing library from the bead-associated state to the illustrated product ready for cluster generation. The product retains its target insert and flanking P5, Index 2, Index 1 and P7 regions. Release chemistry and the fate of the probe are not shown.
operations.information_effect: Recovers enriched RNA-derived DNA/cDNA library inserts for downstream sequence identification. Both indexes remain linked to the insert, supporting assignment to a pooled input library when an index-to-library mapping is available. Capture selects for probe-complementary library sequences; the drawing supplies no sequencing reads, quantitative expression measurement, or evidence of perfect specificity or recovery. Cluster generation and sequencing are downstream interfaces.
